title: Basics
summary: Loops, digits, number tricks and simple conversions

guide.title: Every program is built from these pieces
points: Loops, conditions and arithmetic are what every other topic is made of: arrays, strings and DP are just loops with a smarter plan.
The first online round of most mass recruiters (TCS NQT, Infosys, Wipro, Accenture) has questions on digits, divisibility and number conversions.
Being fast and error-free here gives you time for the harder questions later in the same test.

guide.title: Where you meet this outside an exam
points: Card and ID validation: payment pages check a card number with the Luhn algorithm, which walks the digits one by one.
Money: apps store ₹12.50 as 1250 paise (an integer) so rounding errors never creep into a bill.
Number formatting: showing 1234567 as 12,34,567 in an Indian app is digit splitting.
Binary: file permissions, network masks and colour codes are numbers read in base 2 or 16.

guide.title: Repeat, test, accumulate
points: Keep a variable for the answer you are building (a sum, a count, a reversed number).
Use a loop to look at one piece at a time: a number from 1 to n, or one digit of a number.
n % 10 is the last digit; dividing by 10 (and dropping the fraction) removes it. Repeat while n > 0.
Beginner check: walk through the loop on paper for a tiny input such as 4521 before typing.

guide.title: Sum of digits in your language
points: Same idea in every language; what changes is how integer division is written.
Java and C++ drop the fraction automatically for int / int; JavaScript needs Math.floor; Python uses //.

code.python:
n, total = 4521, 0
while n > 0:
    total += n % 10     # last digit
    n //= 10            # drop it
print(total)            # 12

guide.title: Build a number digit by digit
points: To reverse 1234: take the last digit and append it to the result with result = result × 10 + digit.
The same move converts text to a number ("482" → 482) and builds binary or any other base.

code.python:
n, rev = 1234, 0
while n > 0:
    rev = rev * 10 + n % 10
    n //= 10
# rev = 4321

guide.title: How fast, how big
points: A digit loop runs once per digit: about log₁₀(n) steps, so even 10¹⁸ needs only 18 steps.
A loop from 1 to n is O(n): fine for a million, too slow for 10¹⁸. Look for a formula, e.g. 1 + 2 + … + n = n(n + 1) / 2.
Number sizes: int holds about ±2.1 × 10⁹ in Java and C++; use long / long long beyond that. JavaScript is exact up to 2⁵³; Python integers never overflow.

guide.title: What loses marks
points: Forgetting n = 0: a while (n > 0) loop never runs, so "count the digits of 0" returns 0 instead of 1.
Negative numbers: -7 % 10 is -7 in Java, C++ and JavaScript but 3 in Python. Decide how to treat the sign first.
Division: 5 / 2 is 2.5 in JavaScript and Python, but 2 in Java and C++ (for ints).
Off-by-one: is it i < n or i <= n? Check the first and the last value the loop sees.

guide.title: For advanced learners and interviews
points: Before coding, say the input range aloud and choose int or long; interviewers notice.
Know the shortcuts: digit count = String(n).length or ⌊log₁₀ n⌋ + 1; sum of digits of a big number given as text needs no maths at all.
Try the edge cases every time: 0, 1, the largest value, a negative value, and a number with zeros inside (9000009).
Next step: Arrays, where the same loop walks over many numbers at once.

problems.title: Sum of first N numbers
problems.statement: Return the sum 1 + 2 + ... + n. For n = 0 the sum is 0.

problems.title: Count the digits
problems.statement: Return how many digits the non-negative integer n has.
problems.hint: Divide by 10 until nothing is left. 0 has one digit.

problems.title: Reverse a number
problems.statement: Return the digits of n in reverse order, without leading zeros.
problems.hint: Build the result: result = result * 10 + lastDigit.

problems.title: FizzBuzz
problems.statement: Return an array for the numbers 1..n: "FizzBuzz" for multiples of 15, "Fizz" for multiples of 3, "Buzz" for multiples of 5, otherwise the number itself (as text).

tests.output: 1 2 Fizz 4 Buzz Fizz 7 8 Fizz Buzz 11 Fizz 13 14 FizzBuzz

hiddenTests.output: 1 2 Fizz 4 Buzz Fizz 7 8 Fizz Buzz 11 Fizz 13 14 FizzBuzz 16 17 Fizz 19 Buzz Fizz 22 23 Fizz Buzz 26 Fizz 28 29 FizzBuzz 31

problems.title: Palindrome number
problems.statement: Return true if the integer n reads the same forwards and backwards. Negative numbers are not palindromes.
problems.hint: Compare the number with its reverse.

problems.title: Armstrong number
problems.statement: A number is an Armstrong number when the sum of its digits, each raised to the number of digits, equals the number. Return true or false.
problems.hint: First count the digits, then add each digit raised to that count.

problems.title: Decimal to binary
problems.statement: Return the binary form of the non-negative integer n as a string, without a built-in conversion.
problems.hint: Collect n % 2 and halve n; the bits come out last first.
